mathematical_checkpoints: A proper limiting plane contains an interior point. Interpolation toward that point and then adjustment to the moving plane proves the lower section inclusion; closedness and boundedness prove the upper inclusion.
Compact interior sets eventually belong to the approximating bodies by a strict support-function margin. This justifies the interior approximation rather than assuming it from one-sided containment.
Section volume convergence occurs in a fixed identified (d-1)-dimensional plane; division by a nonzero normal is continuous. In d=1 the H_0 measure is one.
Compact families of proper nonzero-normal planes have positive uniform margins. A violating sequence would converge to a proper plane and contradict the pointwise statement.

Differentiating the exact simplex cap v(1-s)^d at s=1/(d+1) gives (d+1)Gamma_d v. The direction/level neighborhood is chosen before the Hausdorff tolerance, and the latter tolerance is not tied to a small endpoint mass.
